newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook-products struggle in glut.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook-products struggle in glut.

text.p: Refined oil product prices and premiums will struggle to recover in the coming trading week unless India secures larger than expected spot and term supplies from the market, Gulf traders said on Thursday.

Middle distillates, particularly from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, continue to be well supplied and face tough competition in lacklustre Asian and Far East markets from rival Mediterranean barrels, they said.

One of the scarce potential bright points on sellers' horizons was state India Oil Corp's (IOC) spot diesel tender for August deliveries and its term diesel and kerosene for supplies between August and March 1998.

IOC's spot tender is valid till July 4 though traders were expecting the state firm to award much less than the 855,000 tonnes it secured for July imports. Bids for the term contract, are valid till July 6.
"If Indian buying was ever needed, it's now," said a trader.

Gas oil's premium to independent price quotes was talked at 10-20 cents, dipping from a Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's (ADNOC) 0.5 percent sulphur tender for late July loading which was awarded at a 25 cents premium earlier in the week.
ADNOC last month sold an end June loading cargo at 35 cents.
"Saudi (gas oil) cargoes are on the market unable to find a ready buyer," said one Gulf-based trader.
Gas oil was talked at around $20.50 a barrel fob Gulf, up from $19.95 on June 26 but adrift of year high of $31.50.
Traders largely discounted market talk that some refineries in Saudi Arabia had reduced runs in order to stem supplies to the market and help boost sagging margins.
Jet-kerosene was close to losing its premium to quotes, indicated by ADNOC's apparent decision to cancel its jet tender because of poor bids, traders said.
Jet was assessed at $22.80 a barrel fob Gulf.
Fuel oil cargoes and Fujairah bunker spot markets were steady, buoyed by crude's rise and moderate local interest.
380-cst cargoes held at around a $4 discount to quotes and Fujairah 380-cst bunkers were steady at $96-98 a tonne.
Spot market strength was not reflected in official postings by Saudi Aramco and National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) which cut benchmark bunker prices by $1-$1.50 from July 3.
